name: gizza-ai/convert-quotes
summary: Convert quote delimiters in text or code between single, double and curly styles, respecting escapes.

tool.description: Convert the quote delimiters around quoted runs in text or code between styles: single 'x', double "x", curly “x” and ‘x’. Unlike a find-and-replace it parses the text: backslash escapes are respected so \" is never mistaken for a delimiter, a quote that no longer needs escaping is unescaped ("a \" b" -> 'a " b'), a quote that now collides with the new delimiter is escaped (backslash, SQL-style doubling, or left bare), and word-internal apostrophes (don't, it’s, O'Hara) are never treated as quotes. direction=single-to-double|double-to-single|smart-to-double|smart-to-single|auto-to-double|auto-to-single|swap; auto-* normalizes a file that mixes all four styles. An opening quote with no partner is left untouched by default, or reported with on_unbalanced=error. include_report=true adds counts of runs converted, quotes escaped and lone quotes found. Up to 1,000,000 bytes per run.

direction.description: Which delimiters to read and which to write. 'single-to-double' (default) turns 'x' into "x"; 'double-to-single' does the reverse; 'smart-to-double'/'smart-to-single' read curly “x” and ‘x’ runs and emit straight quotes; 'auto-to-double'/'auto-to-single' read every style at once and normalize a mixed file to one delimiter; 'swap' exchanges ' and " in a single pass.

escape_style.description: How to protect a quote that ends up inside the new delimiter. 'backslash' (default) writes \" or \' — the C, JavaScript, Python, JSON, Rust and Go convention; 'doubled' writes "" or '' — the SQL, CSV and Pascal convention; 'bare' leaves the inner quote alone, which is right for prose but produces a broken literal in code.

include_report.description: When true, return JSON with the converted text plus counts: 'converted' quoted runs, inner quotes 'escaped', and 'unbalanced' lone quotes left as-is. Default false returns just the converted text.

input.description: The text or code whose quote delimiters should be converted, e.g. print('hello') or He said “hi”. Everything outside a quoted run is passed through byte for byte. Up to 1,000,000 bytes (1000 KB) per run.

on_unbalanced.description: What to do with an opening quote that has no closing partner. 'keep' (default) leaves that one character exactly as it was and converts the rest; 'error' fails and names the character position, so a malformed file is not half-converted.

preserve_apostrophes.description: When true (default), a ' or ’ sitting between two word characters is an apostrophe, not a delimiter, so don't, it’s and O'Hara survive and 'don't stop' still converts as one run. Set false to treat every single quote as a delimiter.
